biography: Greg Moore, a name once synonymous with raw speed and Canadian motorsport pride, now echoes with a tinge of what-could-have-been. Born in Maple Ridge, British Columbia, Greg's racing journey began with karts, fueled by a childhood spent tearing around the family farm on anything with wheels. His ambition crystallized after witnessing Nigel Mansell's dominant IndyCar season in '93; from that moment, Greg knew his destiny lay on the asphalt. Moore rapidly ascended the open-wheel ranks, showcasing a fearless driving style that both thrilled fans and occasionally terrified his pit crew. After a promising start with Reynard 98i Mercedes, marked by flashes of brilliance and a few too many off-track excursions, his career plateaued. A switch to Mercedes promised a fresh start, but the magic never truly returned. Now, at 34, whispers of retirement circulate, a stark contrast to the roar of expectation that once surrounded him.
drivingStyle: Moore's driving style is best described as a controlled explosion. He possesses an uncanny ability to extract maximum grip from the car, often dancing on the very edge of control. He attacks corners with relentless aggression, favoring late braking and a high corner entry speed. However, this aggressive style also makes him prone to errors, particularly when under pressure. Tire management has never been his strong suit, often sacrificing long-term pace for a few blistering laps. He thrives on adrenaline and the thrill of overtaking, but can sometimes be overly ambitious, leading to costly mistakes.

rivalries.name: Ricardo Diaz
rivalries.reason: A long-standing feud stemming from a controversial collision at Long Beach that cost Diaz the race and Moore a penalty. The two have publicly traded barbs ever since.

rivalries.name: Isabelle Dubois
rivalries.reason: A clash of personalities. Dubois, known for her meticulous and calculated approach, often criticized Moore's reckless abandon on the track, leading to a bitter rivalry both on and off the track.

rivalries.name: Kenji Tanaka
rivalries.reason: Tanaka, a rising star, openly challenged Moore's position as the 'flashiest' driver in the series, resulting in a tense competition to outdo each other in terms of audacious overtakes and lap times.

quirks: Always wears a lucky loon pendant under his racing suit, a gift from his grandmother.
Insists on listening to a specific punk rock song ('Fuel' by Propagandhi) right before getting into the car, regardless of the track or weather.
Refuses to sign autographs with a black pen, believing it brings bad luck.
famousQuote: Second place is just the first loser. Out there, it's kill or be killed.
careerHighlight: Winning the Toronto Indy in 2018, a home victory that sent the Canadian crowd into a frenzy and solidified his status as a national hero for at least one glorious day.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the Indy 500 in 2020 with only five laps to go, a mistake that cost him the biggest win of his career and triggered a wave of intense criticism.
